evidence: Verified at frozen HEAD 3abee5a6add69443e49322e96f9130b834686235 against base 565def869ae50e47e6da7388ea333229050eaf8d. Complete structural reproduction, without executing runtime/tests: (1) A valid V2 pull for seat S obtains the shared owner Arc via src/service/delivery_presentation.rs:57-62; ModChannelRegistry::presentation_owner delegates to the seat-keyed permit cache (src/service/mod_channels.rs:695-697; delivery_presentation.rs:26-47). Its guard stays in scope across canonical store work at :199-216 and post-store progress installation at :281-290. The store writer is acquired by src/store/mod.rs:1303-1314; accepted physical commit time is explicitly unbounded by src/store/connection.rs:330-336, and the commit occurs at :382. Thus A can hold S's permit while storage completes. (2) Dispatch a second structurally valid V2 pull B for S before A finishes. Dispatch routes straight to presentation_pull (src/service/dispatch.rs:1426). B reaches the unconditional std::sync::Mutex::lock at delivery_presentation.rs:62 before either Hook/Watch budget-aware admission (:63-66); confirm has the identical ordering at :298-309. A directly held exact presentation_owner permit gives the same deterministic schedule without requiring a slow disk. (3) Cancel B's token or pass its deadline while A still holds the permit. B cannot return while that permit remains held: fetched official Rust documentation https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/struct.Mutex.html#method.lock states, 'Acquires a mutex, blocking the current thread until it is able to do so.' No budget or cancellation token is passed to lock, and no application budget check can execute during this wait. CallBudget exhaustion is cancellation OR monotonic deadline (src/protocol/time.rs:172-185). The outcome holds even for a budget already cancelled when entering presentation_pull. (4) Through the actual transport, B occupies a blocking worker (src/daemon/transport.rs:491-512). EOF, expiry or shutdown cancels B (:514-528), then the transport awaits that worker (:530-534); the ordinary admission permit remains owned until serve_connection returns (:315-320). B therefore retains both worker and ordinary admission slot until A releases the mutex, regardless of B's cancellation/deadline. Finite concurrent calls for this seat can retain the ordinary pool (MAX_CONNECTIONS=32 at :31; admission :211-214), affecting unrelated requests; claiming data loss or permanent deadlock is unnecessary. (5) This violates the stated preservation contract: finish-capacity-design.md:124 requires retaining cancellation/owner replacement, and TRUST-POLICY.md:1713-1715 explicitly says these allowances add no time-budget extension and weaken no cancellation or exact-owner fence. Serialization itself is authorized (TRUST :1541-1542; capacity design :45; owner-replay design :104 and :152), but none accepts an uncancellable pre-admission waiter. The accepted physical commit/storage-outcome limit (connection.rs:330-336) belongs to A after acceptance, whereas B has not even reached its admission/store decision; allowing B to leave the wait need not disturb A or its fencing guard. This is introduced by this diff: delivery_presentation.rs is a new file absent on the base, and base mod_channels.rs contains no presentation owner permit. The existing base/current store writer wait polls live_budget and uses try_lock with at most 2ms sleeps (base src/store/mod.rs:352-392; current :355-399), so writer contention already allowed cancelled/deadline-expired waiters to finish independently of the holder. Should-fix for avoidable resource retention and availability degradation during overlapping hooks/reconnect activity, with no need to strengthen the accepted commit-time guarantee.
